caption: What if the calendar followed only the Moon? One Moon cycle lasts about 29.5 days, so 12 Moons make about 354 days, 11 short of the Sun's 365. Diwali falls on a new-moon night, which is why it was on 20 October in 2025 but 8 November in 2026. The reason: 2026 got an extra month, Adhik Maas, from 17 May to 15 June. It is added about every 32.5 months to keep festivals in step with the seasons. Delete it and festivals slide about 11 days earlier every year: in about 8 years Diwali would land in the monsoon, in about 16 in peak summer. This already happens with Ramadan: the Hijri year has no extra month, so Ramadan comes 10 to 11 days earlier each year and circles the calendar in about 33 years. Makar Sankranti follows the Sun, so it stays near 14 January. Plot twist: Sanskrit 'mas' meant both moon and month, and English 'month' comes from 'moon'. Which festival would YOU miss most? 👇
